raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old woman with advanced HIV disease (antiretroviral treatment experienced with treatment interruption) presented to Khayelitsha District Hospital with multiple cutaneous abscesses and associated constitutional symptoms of loss of appetite, loss of weight and night sweats. She reported a 3-month history of subcutaneous swellings with overlying hyperpigmentation affecting the arms, legs and buttocks, which subsequently formed spontaneous sinuses with drainage of purulent discharge.
The patient had a history of three previous episodes of drug-sensitive TB and had completed anti-TB treatment on all occasions (Table 1). She had recently been admitted to the surgical department where she was diagnosed with lower limb cellulitis complicated by soft tissue collections. During that admission, an incision and drainage procedure was performed, and the patient received an oral course of amoxicillin and clavulanic acid. Routine microscopy, culture and sensitivity of the pus did not identify any bacterial pathogen; however, a specific mycobacterial culture was not requested.
On admission to the internal medicine department, the patient had a tachycardia and a documented fever. She was cachectic with pallor and generalised lymphadenopathy. She had multiple skin lesions with a widespread distribution, affecting predominantly the lower limbs, perianal area, hands and face. The lower limb and perianal lesions involved subcutaneous collections with overlying hyperpigmented patches and central fluctuance. Certain of these collections had ulcerated with draining sinuses (Figure 1). Her facial lesions were hyperpigmented papules and plaques predominantly affecting the nasal area and associated with crusting suggestive of lupus vulgaris (Figure 2). Initial blood results showed acute kidney impairment, normocytic anaemia and an elevated C-reactive protein (Table 2).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old female presenting with a 3-month history of multiple draining subcutaneous abscesses, anorexia, significant weight loss, and night sweats.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced progressive subcutaneous swellings with overlying hyperpigmentation affecting the upper limbs, lower limbs, and buttocks for 3 months, which subsequently formed spontaneous cutaneous sinuses draining purulent discharge, accompanied by progressive anorexia, weight loss, and drenching night sweats. She was recently admitted to a surgical service for lower limb cellulitis complicated by soft tissue collections, undergoing incision and drainage and oral amoxicillin-clavulanic acid therapy without clinical resolution; routine pus cultures showed no bacterial growth. Due to worsening lesions, she was admitted to internal medicine.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of advanced retroviral disease (antiretroviral treatment experienced with treatment interruption). History of three prior episodes of drug-sensitive tuberculosis, completing full anti-TB therapy on all occasions. Recent incision and drainage of lower extremity soft tissue collections treated with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for anorexia, weight loss, night sweats, localized extremity skin pain and drainage; negative for acute chest pain, hemoptysis, or shortness of breath. Home medications: unmentioned. Allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: tachycardia and documented pyrexia/fever. General appearance: cachectic, marked pallor, generalized lymphadenopathy. Dermatologic: widespread lesions predominantly involving the lower extremities, perianal area, hands, and face; lower limb and perianal lesions demonstrated subcutaneous collections with overlying hyperpigmented patches, central fluctuance, and ulcerations with actively draining sinuses; facial lesions consisted of crusted hyperpigmented papules and plaques across the nasal bridge resembling lupus vulgaris.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: normocytic anemia; serum chemistry: acute kidney impairment; inflammatory markers: elevated C-reactive protein (CRP). Prior pus routine microscopy, culture, and sensitivity: no bacterial pathogen isolated.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated cutaneous tuberculosis presenting with metastatic tuberculous abscesses (tuberculous gummas) and lupus vulgaris-like facial plaques in advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with antiretroviral interruption. Pyogenic bacterial infection ruled out by negative routine pus cultures. Management & Outcome: Patient previously failed incision, drainage, and empiric amoxicillin-clavulanic acid. Clinical features of chronic draining sinuses, lupus vulgaris plaques, constitutional B-symptoms, and prior history of recurrent TB in an immunocompromised host established disseminated cutaneous tuberculosis, warranting reinstitution of anti-tuberculosis therapy and subsequent resumption of combination antiretroviral therapy.
